item.text: {"question_id":"8B.8","answer":"For 2023, the evidence supports selective institutional change and some formal corrective machinery, but not a reliably demonstrated presidential feedback loop from audits or failures to improved results. The federal health system was reorganized through IMSS-BIENESTAR rules that required supervision, monitoring, corrective measures, evaluations, public reporting, and follow-up on recommendations (BATCH-0051-E001; BATCH-0051-E004; BATCH-0051-E005). The government also launched a centralized medicine warehouse as López Obrador’s response to persistent shortages, although delivery performance was not yet established and the preceding transition was associated with sharply worse reported access to health services (BATCH-0013-E006; BATCH-0032-E003). Project designs were repeatedly changed, including Tren Maya Section 5, and some changes were presented as responses to environmental or technical risks; however, critics reported inadequate studies, legal noncompliance, and improvised implementation, so adaptation cannot be equated with effective learning (BATCH-0011-E007). Personnel changes followed the Segalmex investigation, but Ovalle was reassigned to another government post, weakening the case that failure led to accountable replacement (BATCH-0046-E008). In the search system, the executive announced a recount, the commission head resigned, and a replacement was appointed, but the lower revised total and concerns about transparency, consultation, and experience make corrective intent and competence uncertain (BATCH-0004-E008). Broader monitoring evidence is adverse: CONEVAL reported that recommendations were disregarded to varying degrees, several priority programs lacked results measurement or required major indicator and logical-design improvements, and 53% of monitored six-year indicators were insufficient, lagging, or very lagging (BATCH-0052-E004; BATCH-0052-E006; BATCH-0054-E005). The World Bank also recorded cancellations, dropped projects, changing priorities, and restructurings that could represent either adaptation or implementation failure, with attribution shared across government, institutional, budgetary, and implementation factors (BATCH-0052-E020). Nuclear corrective systems show operational learning within CFE/CNSNS, but lack direct López Obrador attribution and therefore should not be treated as presidential adaptation (BATCH-0002-E004; BATCH-0002-E010; BATCH-0002-E012). Overall, adaptation was observable in redesigns, institutional turnover, and formal monitoring architecture, but evidence that the ruler consistently used findings to replace ineffective implementers, reallocate resources, and produce verified improvement remains
